AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: Microsurgical denervation of the spermatic cord (MDSC) is a treatment option for chronic orchialgia that is refractory to conservative treatment. A recent study has shown specific nerve fibers as the possible cause of chronic orchialgia. Our goal was to present outcomes of ligation of these nerves using a targeted robotic assisted microsurgical denervation of the spermatic cord (TRMDSC) technique.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS AND MATERIALS
AbstractText.content: Retrospective review of 872 cases (772 patients) who underwent TRMDSC from Oct 2007 to July 2016. Selection criteria were as follows: chronic testicular pain (>3 months), failed conservative treatments, negative neurologic and urologic workup, and temporary resolution of pain with local anesthetic spermatic cord block. TRMDSC was performed. Pain was assessed preoperatively and postoperatively using the subjective visual analog scale (VAS) and objectively with the standardized validated pain score (PIQ-6 by RAND).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Follow up data was available in 860 cases. Over a median f/u of 24 months (1-70), 83% (718 cases) had a significant reduction in pain and 17% (142 cases) had no change in pain by subjective VAS scoring. Within the patients who had significant reduction in pain: 49 % (426 cases) had complete resolution and 34% (292 cases) had a >=50% reduction in pain. Objective PIQ-6 analysis showed a significant reduction in pain in: 67% at 6 months, 68% at 1 year, 77% at 2 years, 86% at 3 years, 83% at 4 years post-op.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: TRMDSC is an effective, minimally invasive approach with potential long- term durability for patients with refractory chronic orchialgia.
